main_text.p: Caulibus instillet. Plinius phaginorum meminit. & gutti lignei mentio est in vita M. Curij Dentali, apud eum scriptorem veterem, cuius extat De viris illustribus liber. Fiebant & è corio: nam ampullarum οχυλινων, id est, scortearum meminere Hippocrates, Plautus, Festus, alij. Has Graeci ὀλκας proprie vocabant. Scholiastes Theocriti, idyllio secundo, Ὀλκη ξυεῖος ἢ διφθερτίνη λαικυ, εἰ ἢ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἔλαιον. De his coriaceis ammpullis intelligendum quod ait Plutarchus in Sylla, Athenienses obsessos ἐρπιδάμα & λακυδές ἐφέδες comedisse. Plerique aereis utebantur & quidem Corinthiacis, ut notat idem Scholiastes. Sed & argenteas λακυδές ditiores habuerunt. Theocritus,

[illegible, ~8 letters]Frequentissimo vero ut opinor in usu erant lecythi operis figlini: ut Campani gutti apud Horatium: & Samij, quorum multi meminerunt. Nam fere Samia vasa testacea erant: etsi scio fuisse apud Samios etiam ligneorum vasorum nobiles artifices, vel tcste Cicerone epistola quadam ad Q. fratrem.

καὶ βαλανείας.] Mirificè hæc conveniunt ei quem hic describit Theophrastus: ei inquam, qui omnibus in rebus [illegible, ~8 letters] volunt habere vult videri: cuiusmodi hominum observavimus morem illis temporibus fuisse ut baculum gererent. Demosthenes adversus Pantænetum: Νικλέους ἀλλ' ἐπιφέρεται, καὶ [illegible, ~10 letters] τρία notat summus orator, quæ vulgò invidiam conflare solerent: citatum ingressum: vocem altam: baculi

page.notes: Printed lines in italics or Greek were read as far as the scan allows; the Greek lines and the Greek words marked illegible are not reliable and need checking against a better scan. The left margin note at the top reads "Caulibus instillet." The margin note beside the Frequentissimo paragraph is a Greek word that could not be read and is marked illegible. The first Greek margin note beside the Mirifice paragraph is most likely "καὶ βαλανείας.]". The abbreviation "Q ," in the Frequentissimo paragraph is printed as shown. The Greek line between the Theocritus paragraph and the Frequentissimo paragraph is set apart and may be a quotation.
